name: Lastlea

side.hint: Push the stick to walk, A to jump, B to talk. Push it up or down at an arrow to cross to another lane.

hints: The Answer has what it asked for, and Lastlea is thriving.
Wren walks with you. Lastlea has gone cold. The Answer is waiting.
Wren's echo is with you. The Answer waits in the cathedral, down the road from the south gate.
The hall is quiet. The door under the bluff now leads on down, to the Dark Stair.
Tap the open door to go down and fight.
Take the brass key to the door under the bluff: north past the well, then west.
Find the chest beyond the pond.
Talk to the elder by the well. The road out of the south gate leads to the cathedral.
You are the Lastmade, sent by the Answer. Tap the ground to walk. Tap people to talk.

case: My knee stopped aching this morning. Twenty years it ached. I don't ask questions of a gift.
Feathers came down off every door, too. Wind, I expect. There was no wind.
The hearths would not take last night. The whole village slept cold. First time in my life.
Something small ran past my gate, laughing. I did not look. I have a rule about not looking.
Quiet under the bluff, they say. I never doubted the Answer would send someone.
Welcome to Lastlea. Quiet place. The Answer has always seen to that.
If you hear humming up by the bluff at night, that is the stair door. Shut since little Wren's day.
One of the Answer's own, walking in at my gate! Welcome to Lastlea. Quiet place. The Answer has always seen to that.
If you hear humming up by the bluff at night, that is the stair door. Shut since little Wren's day.
And mind the pale thing drifting about north of the west house. It came out with the humming.
The bells rang themselves at dawn, and the well runs sweet for the first time in years. Bless you, child.
The feathers all came down off the doors in the night. We will pin up new ones for Wrenfeast. He would have liked that.
The well has gone slow, and the bread will not rise. The Answer is quiet with us. I do not know what we have done.
And Pip says she heard a boy singing by the well. There is no boy that age in Lastlea. There has not been for a long time.
You are back! Did you see his lamp niches, down there? He kept every one of them filled, our Wren.
He flew, you know. I was there. The Answer bore him up like a leaf.
You have a look about you. Did you find his shrine, down there?
They say he was smiling when he leapt. I have always liked that part.
Quiet under the bluff again. You have done us a kindness.
Do you know our Wren? A lamp-boy, no higher than my hip. The night the bluff cracked he leapt from the top to warn the village, and the Answer bore him up like a leaf.
We pin up paper feathers for him every year. It is nearly Wrenfeast now.
The door is open. The Answer go with you. It always has.
You found the key! Then north past the well and west, under the bluff. Wren keep you.
Oh! One of the Answer's own, here in Lastlea. Forgive an old woman for staring. We prayed, and here you are.
You will want the stair under the bluff. It has been shut since little Wren's day, and lately it hums.
The miller keeps its brass key in a chest beyond the pond. Would you fetch it? My knees are not what they were.

choose: Bless you. Look beyond the pond, where the reeds grow thick.
Of course. I will be by the well when you change your mind.

case: The bells rang themselves, and now all Lastlea wants a feather. I sold out by noon.
Odd thing. Every one I hung last night was lying face down this morning. I hung new ones.
Nobody is buying feathers. They say the Answer has turned its face from us.
I say it is the weather. I have said it four times today.
Paper feathers! One prayer each. No, I jest, take one. It is nearly Wrenfeast.
The old ledges behind my stall go up to the mill, and to Wren's Leap, if your knees are younger than mine.
I asked Elder Maren if Wren is happy now. She said to go and play.
Everyone is cold. There is a boy who hums by the well, and he is not cold.
He would not say his name. He knew mine.
You found the shiny thing! I knew it was there.
I made a feather for Wrenfeast. Mine has the most glue.
There is something shiny in the reeds past the pond. I saw it glint!
Are you an angel? Elder Maren says not to ask.

then: WREN'S LEAP, says the worn stone by the mill door. HERE THE CHILD FLEW.
The miller's crate is empty now. The sails creak round overhead.
else: A worn stone is set by the mill door: WREN'S LEAP. HERE THE CHILD FLEW.
Beside it sits a crate with the miller's mark, left for whoever climbs up at Wrenfeast.
You take two Tonics. All of Lastlea lies below, small and warm.

case: The stair drops into the dark. The hall below is quiet now, and a second stair goes on down past it.
The stair drops into the dark. Something is moving down there.
A heavy door, sealed tight. Paper feathers are pinned all around its frame.
The brass key turns with a heavy clunk.
The door swings open. Cold air rolls up from the dark, and the paper feathers stir.

road: The road forks beyond the gate.

choose: The pilgrim road, to the cathedral
The road climbs between old hedges toward the spires.
The shore road, to Lighthouse rock
The shore road runs down to a rowboat pulled up on the shingle.
You push off toward the light on the rock.
